title: Exploring Flat Minima for Domain Generalization With Large Learning Rates
venue: IEEE Transactions on Knowledge and Data Engineering
publication_status_observed: arXiv preprint arXiv:2309.06337v1, submitted to IEEE TKDE
main_claims: Large learning rates promote weight diversity and help models escape sharp local minima, thereby improving domain generalization.
The Lookahead training strategy (fast-slow weight interpolation) enables the use of large learning rates without convergence failure by blending fast unconverged weights with slow stable weights.
Weight interpolation implicitly optimizes a local entropy objective that measures flatness, providing a principled connection between Lookahead and flat minima.
methodology: The authors provide a theoretical analysis showing that distributional shift is equivalent to weight-space perturbations, then argue that flat minima are necessary for robustness to domain shift. Lookahead uses a large learning rate for k inner-loop steps with fast weights, then interpolates with slow weights at ratio α. Two regularized variants (AvgLookahead, RegLookahead) are proposed to prevent overfitting. Experiments cover PACS, VLCS, OfficeHome, TerraIncognita, and DomainNet classification, plus semantic segmentation DG benchmarks. Feature diversity is measured with CKA, and prediction diversity is measured with Ndiff/Nsimul.
key_results: Large learning rate (5e-4) produces lower CKA feature similarity (0.7882 vs 0.9822 in-domain) compared to small learning rate (5e-5), indicating greater weight diversity.
Lookahead-based methods achieve state-of-the-art performance on DomainBed classification and semantic segmentation DG benchmarks.
Models trained with larger learning rates converge to flatter loss surfaces on PACS as visualized by 1D loss curves, confirming the flat-minima hypothesis.
limitations: Flat-minima measurements rely on loss landscape visualizations rather than Hessian eigenvalues or SAM-style neighborhood loss, limiting quantitative comparability.
The equivalence of distributional shift to weight perturbations (Theorem 1) holds only approximately and under specific assumptions about distribution proximity.
Does not include CIFAR-C/ImageNet-C corruption benchmarks; CKA diversity analysis is not explicitly linked to OOD accuracy via correlation or regression.
relevance_to_rq: Directly relevant: proposes a weight-averaging-based flat-minima method (Lookahead) analogous to SWA, uses CKA to measure feature diversity (not paired-image CKA stability), and demonstrates flat minima benefit DG. Provides context for the SWA flat-minima control in the RQ's experimental design.

extraction_issues: evidence_strength is mixed: flat-minima measurements are demonstrative (loss landscape plots), while DG benchmark results are empirical comparisons without causal isolation. The CKA diversity measurement is correlational.
